source.title: Large-Scale Distributed Second-Order Optimization Using Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature for Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
source.authors: Kazuki Osawa; Yohei Tsuji; Yuichiro Ueno; Akira Naruse; Rio Yokota; S. Matsuoka

record.tranche_reason: The study trains ResNet-50 with K-FAC across large batch sizes and reports validation accuracy, examining whether the large-batch generalization penalty persists under its optimizer and training recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its K-FAC training outcomes across batch sizes and several K-FAC training-scheme comparisons. Comparisons in Table 2 from other work are cited results, not rows. Fisher-matrix staleness measurements describe optimizer state, not a tested generalization-gap measure.
record.test_reason: The study varies batch size and reports ImageNet validation accuracy using K-FAC and an adapted training recipe. Its results bear on V5's recipe-dependent exceptions, although they do not isolate a fixed-epoch batch-size penalty.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that their distributed K-FAC recipes achieve competitive ImageNet validation accuracy at extremely large batch sizes and converge with fewer epochs or iterations than cited SGD recipes. Their SGD comparison uses published reference results, rather than a controlled optimizer comparison, and does not establish equal accuracy against every reference.
record.recipe_differences: Uses second-order K-FAC with damping, running mixup, random erasing, learning-rate and momentum schedules, and weight rescaling; not the original large-batch SGD recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size is varied; training hyperparameters differ by batch size. The paper also reports K-FAC accuracy comparisons across Fisher-information approximations at batch size 32,768.

fits_no_version.finding: Diagonal Fisher approximation preserves validation curves, including when combined with stale Fisher information, at batch size 32,768.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: K-FAC Fisher approximations can reduce computational overhead while preserving validation performance.

record.problems: No controlled small-batch K-FAC comparison is reported; batch-size conditions use different hyperparameters and epoch counts. Validation accuracy is reported, but training error is not, so the training-to-test gap itself is not measured. Very large batches are mimicked by gradient accumulation.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 lists results from related work, which are cited comparisons rather than this study's own results. Figure 5 reports Fisher-factor change rates, which measure optimizer-state variation rather than the generalization gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive methods versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; comparisons with SGD are external reference results.
An unchanged-recipe fixed-epoch penalty; a controlled comparison showing how much adaptation removes that penalty; small-batch K-FAC baselines; language models.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and rankings against other measures.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V5. Different epoch budgets are an untested comparison, not independently a limits_scope verdict. Table 2 also contains this study's own 74.9% stale-Fisher run; the record incorrectly describes the whole table as cited results. That run measures optimizer implementation performance at a single batch size and adds no distinct batch-size comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold is not varied.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures are not compared.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning are not tested.

The paper tests large-batch outcomes with K-FAC, not SGD; its batch-size configurations use differing hyperparameters, and it does not compare the same epoch budget across batch sizes as a controlled test.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps are not measured.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet with K-FAC using mini-batch size 4,096.
rows.note: Natural-label validation accuracy reported for a large-batch K-FAC run.
rows.check: The value is correct, but this is the smallest-batch reference: 75.1 ± 0.09% at 35 epochs. Alone it cannot establish a batch-size penalty.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet with K-FAC using mini-batch size 8,192.
rows.note: Natural-label validation accuracy reported for a large-batch K-FAC run.
rows.check: No validation penalty relative to R1: 75.2 ± 0.05% versus 75.1 ± 0.09%, both at 35 epochs. Hyperparameters differ by batch size.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet with K-FAC using mini-batch size 16,384.
rows.note: Natural-label validation accuracy reported for a large-batch K-FAC run.
rows.check: No validation penalty relative to R1: 75.2 ± 0.03% versus 75.1 ± 0.09%, both at 35 epochs. Hyperparameters differ by batch size.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet with K-FAC using mini-batch size 32,768.
rows.note: Natural-label validation accuracy reported for a large-batch K-FAC run.
rows.check: Correct value; bears on V5's adapted-recipe clause. Accuracy reaches 75.3 ± 0.13% with 45 epochs, versus 35 epochs for R1–R3. It cannot establish the fixed-epoch penalty or quantify its removal.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet with K-FAC using mini-batch size 65,536.
rows.note: Natural-label validation accuracy reported for a large-batch K-FAC run.
rows.check: Correct value; bears on V5's adapted-recipe clause. Accuracy reaches 75.0 ± 0.09% with 60 epochs and batch-specific hyperparameters. It cannot establish the fixed-epoch penalty or quantify its removal.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet with K-FAC using mini-batch size 131,072.
rows.note: The authors note this batch size had fewer than 10 iterations per epoch.
rows.check: Correct value; bears on V5's adapted-recipe clause. Accuracy reaches 75.0 ± 0.06% with 100 epochs and batch-specific hyperparameters. It cannot establish the fixed-epoch penalty or quantify its removal.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet with K-FAC at mini-batch size 32,768 and diagonal Fisher information for Batch Normalization layers.
rows.baseline: The same training curve with K-FAC plotted in Figure 3 (no approx)
rows.value: Figure 6: diag; the authors state the diagonal approximation does not affect the training curve.
rows.note: No separate numerical accuracy is stated for this scheme.
rows.check: Compares Fisher approximations at one batch size, measuring the proposed optimizer's performance rather than a batch-size effect. The text supports unchanged validation curves under diagonal approximation.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet at mini-batch size 32,768 using stale Fisher information for all layers.
rows.baseline: The same training curve with K-FAC plotted in Figure 3 (no approx)
rows.value: Figure 6: stale; the text does not separately state its accuracy effect.
rows.note: The text discusses whether diagonal FIM affects the training curve but gives no explicit statement about the stale-only curve.
rows.check: Compares Fisher-refresh schemes at one batch size; it does not measure any claim version. The supplied figure text does not expose numerical curve values.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Train on ImageNet at mini-batch size 32,768 with both diagonal and stale Fisher information.
rows.baseline: The same training curve with K-FAC plotted in Figure 3 (no approx)
rows.value: Figure 6: stale_diag; no separate numerical accuracy stated.
rows.note: The paper states diagonal FIM does not affect the curve even with stale FIM, but gives no quantified separate result.
rows.check: Compares Fisher approximations at one batch size; it does not measure any claim version. The explicit unchanged-curve statement concerns adding diagonal approximation with or without staleness.

relationships.condition: Adapted K-FAC recipes at batch sizes 4,096–16,384 with a common 35-epoch budget
relationships.reason: R1–R3 report 75.1%, 75.2%, and 75.2% validation accuracy, supporting V5's exception that adapted image-classification recipes can avoid a penalty within the same epoch budget.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest that adapted recipes using K-FAC, an optimizer that approximates loss curvature, retained similar validation accuracy within the common epoch budget.

relationships.condition: K-FAC at batch sizes 32,768–131,072 with batch-specific recipes and longer training
relationships.reason: R4–R6 retain approximately 75% accuracy using 45, 60, and 100 epochs, consistent with V5's adaptation clause; no unchanged-recipe control establishes how much penalty was removed.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest similar accuracy with larger batches and longer training, without unchanged-recipe controls establishing recovery.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet-50 on ImageNet trained with K-FAC at mini-batch sizes 4,096 through 131,072
reader_labels.reason: The reported validation accuracies remain at about 75% across the batch-size sweep (R1–R6), and the authors report that K-FAC retains competitive accuracy at the largest batch.
